answer:
HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded):

"Urban land use promoted a specific type of plant invasion by favouring UNINTENTIONALLY introduced species (contaminant/hitchhiking weeds) over ornamental garden-escapees. In the Barcelona-province plot network (632 plots), holding habitat type, cropland cover and elevation constant, increasing urban cover in the surroundings shifts the pathway mix toward Unintentional invaders and away from Gardening invaders: the urban effect on counts differs between the two pathways by b = −1.15 (SE 0.54, p = 0.032) for the primary exposure urban.2009.50m — i.e., going from a non-urban to a fully urban surrounding multiplies the expected number of Unintentional-invader records relative to Gardening-invader records by ≈3.2× (Gardening itself does not gain: its urban coefficient is negative, IRR ≈ 0.61). This direction is stable across ALL 9 buffer×year combinations (Gardening-minus-Unintentional contrast negative in 9/9; significant in 6/9, strongest and most significant at the broader 500–1000 m buffers, e.g. urban.1956.500m contrast = −2.80, p = 0.009; urban.2009.1000m = −2.19, p = 0.007), so the conclusion is robust to the choice of buffer/period. Descriptively, in plots classified as 'Urban' habitat the Unintentional share of recorded invaders is 68.9% vs 29.8% Gardening (and 76.9% in Croplands), whereas Gardening invaders dominate in Wetlands (55.8%), forests (87.5–100%) and Coastal plots (53.5%). Species-level data agree: unintentionally introduced species occupy broader invaded niches (median 0.83 vs 0.38, Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.047) and more plots, remaining significant after phylogenetic correction (PGLS on log1p(#invaded plots): Unintentional b = +1.44, p = 1.6e-05; niche breadth b = +0.46, p = 0.011; residence time positive, p = 0.028). The temporal baseline shows WHY this is a selective, not a supply, effect: Gardening introductions rose from 17% (Before 1500) to 75% (1985–2019) of the Catalonia introduction pool (χ² = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6e-47), yet established urban invasions are still dominated by unintentional introductions — urban land use filters establishment in favour of the Unintentional invasion type. Scenario summary: urbanization — both contemporary urban cover (2009) and cumulative urban presence at landscape scales (500–1000 m buffers) — promotes the invasion type associated with accidental introduction routes (generalist weeds with broad invaded niches), not the ornamental/horticultural invasion type."

WORKFLOW (executed, see analysis.py + outputs/analysis_results.txt):
1. Parsing & audit (TAB vs comma CSVs; no missing values in D and S; n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo = n.total in 100% of rows; change-columns are buffer-area proportions summing to ≈1 with rounding artifacts).
2. Descriptives: pathway totals n.gard=169, n.unint=289, n.agfo=23; only 191/632 plots invaded; shares by habitat; Mann–Whitney for top-urban (urban.2009.50m ≥ 0.01, n=160) vs rest: n.unint 1.00 vs 0.27 (p=1e-21), n.gard 0.59 vs 0.16 (p=4e-16), n.agfo ns (p=0.06).
3. CORE (researcher-designated): long-format count model (632×3 rows) ~ C(pathway)×(urban + cropland + elevation) + C(habitat), Poisson GLM with plot-cluster-robust SE (Pearson χ²/df = 1.18 → no NB needed). Interaction unint×urban b = +0.665 (p = 0.035); urban main (Gardening reference) b = −0.489 (p = 0.091); contrast Gardening−Unintentional = −1.154 (p = 0.032), Gardening−AgriForest = −0.453 (p = 0.48).
4. Hurdle (presence/absence logits): no significant presence effect for gard (OR 0.80, p = 0.66) or unint (OR 1.51, p = 0.47) at 50 m — urban effect acts on abundance, not presence, and is pathway-contrast-specific.
5. Sensitivity (pre-declared, not fishing): 9 urban variables (50/500/1000 m × 1956/1993/2009) — gard−unint contrast negative 9/9, significant 6/9.
6. Confirmatory change analysis (50 m): progressive/regressive 1956–2009 not significant for gard/unint (only AgriForest–regressive p = 0.015, and delta-urban→AgriForest p = 0.048 with only 23 total AgriForest records — treated as weak/unstable, not headline).
7. Species level (n = 81 rows incl. 4 duplicated species): KW tests + phylogenetic GLS (own Newick parser; V = root-to-MRCA depth; all 81 tip labels matched).
8. Temporal context (Catalonia contingency table): χ² and trend shares.

Assumptions honored as agreed: urban.* = share of urban land cover in buffer (radii read as 500/1000 m despite doc typos); change-columns = area proportions; duplicates = two introduction events (kept, distinct phylo tips); no direct species↔plot join exists (D has no species names), so steps 3 and 5 are complementary views, not a joint fit.

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use promoted the invasion type associated with UNINTENTIONAL introduction (contaminant/hitchhiker weeds) rather than ornamental Gardening escapees: controlling for habitat, cropland and elevation, higher urban cover around plots shifts the pathway mix toward Unintentional invaders (Gardening-vs-Unintentional urban contrast b=-1.15, SE 0.54, p=0.032 at urban.2009.50m; direction negative in 9/9 buffer-year combinations, significant in 6/9, strongest at 500-1000 m buffers, e.g. -2.80, p=0.009 at urban.1956.500m). In Urban-habitat plots the Unintentional share of invaders is 68.9% vs 29.8% Gardening. Unintentionally introduced species also occupy broader invaded niches (median 0.83 vs 0.38, KW p=0.047) and more plots (phylogeny-corrected PGLS b=+1.44, p<0.001), although Gardening dominates the introduction pool temporally (share 17%->75% of introductions, 1985-2019 vs Before-1500; chi2=230.4, p<1e-46). Scenario: urban land use - contemporary cover (2009) and cumulative landscape-scale urban presence (>=500 m buffers) - filters establishment in favour of unintentionally introduced, niche-broad generalists over garden-escape ornamentals.
payload.workflow: 1) Parsing/audit (TAB-sep CSVs, no NAs in plot/species tables, pathway-count identity holds 100%, change-columns are proportions summing ~1). 2) Descriptives by habitat and urban quartile (MWU). 3) CORE pre-registered test: long-format counts (632 plots x 3 pathways), Poisson GLM C(pathway)*(urban+cropland+elevation)+C(habitat), cluster-robust SE by plot (Pearson chi2/df=1.18); interaction and Wald contrasts. 4) Hurdle logits for presence (ns - effect is on abundance). 5) Pre-declared sensitivity across 9 urban buffers x years (stable direction 9/9). 6) Confirmatory landscape-change models (progressive/regressive 1956-2009, delta-urban vs delta-cropland). 7) Species-level success by pathway (Kruskal-Wallis) + phylogenetic GLS with covariance from the supplied Newick tree (all 81 tip labels matched). 8) Temporal trends chi-square as supply-side context. Interpretation caveats: urban.* read as share of urban land cover (radii 500/1000 m despite doc typos); change-columns read as area proportions; 4 duplicated species kept as separate introduction events; no species-plot join possible (no species names in plot table); niche-breadth calculation method and plot-selection protocol unknown.
